body_ar: قال الله تعالى يا ابن آدم لو أتيتني بقراب الأرض خطايا يا ابن آدم هذا خطاب للجنس البشري كله، لو أتيتني بقراب الأرض أي بملئها خطايا أي سيئات ثم لقيتني أي مت لا تشرك بي شيئا هذا حال معناه مت على عدم الشرك مت على التوحيد لأتيتك بقرابها مغفرة، لأتيتك أي لكافأتك بقرابها بقراب الأرض أي بملئها مغفرة، والإتيان هنا المقصود به القدوم على الله سبحانه وتعالى، لو أتيتني بقراب الأرض خطايا، المقصود به أن الإنسان إذا مات سيأتي يحمل طائره إذا حشر
body_en: God, exalted is He, said: 'O son of Adam, were you to come to Me with the earth's fill of sins...' — 'O son of Adam': this is an address to the whole human race. 'Were you to come to Me with the earth's fill' — that is, with as much as would fill it — 'of sins', that is, of wrongdoings, 'then meet Me' — that is, were you to die — 'associating nothing with Me' — this is a circumstantial clause, meaning: were you to die free of associating partners with God (shirk), were you to die upon the oneness of God (tawḥīd) — 'I would come to you with the like of it in forgiveness.' 'I would come to you' means: I would requite you; 'with the like of it', that is, with the earth's fill, 'in forgiveness'. What is meant by 'coming' here is presenting oneself before God, glorified and exalted. 'Were you to come to Me with the earth's fill of sins' — what is meant by it is that when a person dies he will come bearing his record of deeds (ţāʾir) when he is gathered

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.context: المقصود به أن الإنسان إذا مات سيأتي يحمل طائره إذا حشر
options: bearing his portion, whatever his deeds have fastened to him
bearing his omen — the fate his own actions have made
flags.note: طائر echoes Q 17:13, وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه, where the exegetes divide between 'record of deeds' and 'destiny/portent'. The Sheikh does not say which he intends, and the sentence breaks off before he explains. The rendering should not settle a question he left open.

options: an amount approaching the whole earth
nearly enough to fill the earth
flags.note: The Sheikh glosses قراب himself as ملء ('a fill'), so option 0 follows his own gloss; lexically قراب carries a sense of 'close to, approaching'. Option 0 is preferred because it is his reading, not the translator's.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.

The passage is a line-by-line gloss of a divine saying (ḥadīth qudsī). The lemmas being glossed have been set in quotation marks in the English so that the Sheikh's commentary is not mistaken for the text of the report; the Arabic source runs the two together without punctuation.
The Sheikh gives no narrator or collection for this report, and none has been supplied.
